parameters.query:
SELECT id, external_id, title, department, locations, description
FROM jobs
WHERE classified_at IS NULL
  AND closed_at IS NULL
  AND classification_attempts < 3
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 150;

parameters.jsCode:
// Arma el pedido de clasificacion para cada aviso que todavia no tiene categoria.
//
// La entrada son filas de la base (Read unclassified): el criterio es
// "classified_at IS NULL", asi que lo que falla se reintenta solo en la
// corrida siguiente y el backfill se drena sin tarea aparte.
//
// El nodo "Classify (Gemini)" lee de este body dos cosas:
//   body.contents[0].parts[0].text        -> el Prompt
//   body.systemInstruction.parts[0].text  -> el System Message
//
// Las listas son las de taxonomia.md y locations-with-ai.md. Si cambian ahi,
// cambian aca, y hay que subir TAXONOMY_VERSION.
//
// OJO: las listas viven en TRES lugares y tienen que decir lo mismo:
// el SYSTEM de abajo, el SCHEMA de abajo, y las constantes del nodo
// "Parse classification".
//
// v2: se agrega la geografia (work_mode, countries, regions). El pipeline
// guarda hechos; el usuario filtra.

const TAXONOMY_VERSION = 2;

const SYSTEM = `You classify job postings for a job board that centralizes jobs relevant to people in Latin America: remote jobs open to the region, and on-site or hybrid jobs located in it.

Choose values ONLY from the lists below. Never invent a value.

job_function — pick exactly one:
  engineering  software, data engineering, ML engineering, SRE, DevOps, QA, security, architecture
  product      product management, product operations
  design       UX, UI, product design, user research, brand, graphic
  marketing    growth, content, demand generation, brand, SEO, communications
  sales        account executive, SDR, sales engineering, partnerships, account management
  operations   business operations, finance, legal, HR / people, logistics, administration
  support      customer support, customer success, technical support
  other        anything that fits none of the above, including non-tech roles such as
               field work, retail, manufacturing, healthcare, drivers, data labeling

  The words after each function are EXAMPLES, not an exhaustive list. Generalize
  from them: a role that is not listed still belongs to the closest function.

  Judge by what the person actually does all day, NOT by which words appear in
  the title. A title can contain the name of a function it does not belong to:
    Product Engineer          -> engineering
    Growth Engineer           -> engineering
    Design Engineer           -> engineering
    Forward Deployed Engineer -> engineering
    Sales Engineer            -> sales       (pre-sales: technical but commercial)
    Solutions Engineer        -> sales       unless the posting shows they build
                                             the product itself
    Support Engineer          -> support
    Product Designer          -> design
    Product Marketing Manager -> marketing
    Product Operations        -> product

  Management roles belong to the function of the team they manage, NOT to a
  separate management category:
    Engineering Manager  -> job_function: engineering, level: manager
    Sales Director       -> job_function: sales,       level: director
    Head of Design       -> job_function: design,      level: manager
    VP of Product        -> job_function: product,     level: vp

level — pick exactly one, based on SCOPE, not on the words in the title:
  junior    0-2 years, "junior", "associate", "entry level", intern
  mid       3-5 years, no seniority word in the title
  senior    "senior", or a clearly senior individual contributor
  staff     "staff", "principal", "distinguished" — an individual contributor
            ABOVE senior, with scope across teams, but WITHOUT direct reports
  lead      HAS DIRECT REPORTS or owns a team's delivery
  manager   "manager", "head of", manages a team
  director  "director", manages other managers
  vp        "VP", "chief", C-level
  unknown   the posting gives no reliable signal about seniority

  CRITICAL: a "Tech Lead" with no direct reports is senior or staff, NOT lead.
  An "Engineering Lead" who manages people is lead. The description decides,
  not the title.

  Use "unknown" honestly. A bare "Software Engineer" with no description is
  unknown, NOT mid. Only answer mid when the posting actually points there.

tags — zero or more, only from this list:
  backend, frontend, fullstack, mobile, infra, data, ml, ai, security, qa, sap, salesforce

  Three of these are easy to confuse:
    ml    training, fine-tuning or evaluating models; MLOps; data science pipelines
    ai    building on top of existing foundation models: prompting, RAG, agents,
          LLM-powered features inside a product
    data  data engineering, pipelines, warehouses, analytics, BI

  fullstack already means backend and frontend: do not add those two next to it.
  A role can carry both ml and ai when it genuinely does both. Management roles
  usually carry no tags at all. Leave tags empty when the posting gives you
  nothing to go on — do not guess.

suggested_tags — technologies, tools, platforms or programming languages that
  are clearly central to this posting but are NOT in the tag list above.
  Free text, lowercase, at most 3.
  Examples: python, terraform, kubernetes, shopify, servicenow, hubspot
  Do NOT put industries (fintech), skills (negotiation) or areas of work
  (compliance, partnerships) here: only things a person learns to use.
  Leave it empty when nothing qualifies. This field never reaches the
  filters — it only feeds a monthly review of what the taxonomy is missing.

work_mode — pick exactly one:
  remote    the job can be done fully away from an office
  hybrid    some days in an office, some away
  onsite    the person must work from a specific office or site
  unknown   the posting does not say

countries — where the person can be based, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes in
  UPPERCASE: ["AR"], ["BR","MX"].
    - onsite or hybrid: the country of the office
    - remote restricted to certain countries: those countries
    - remote open worldwide or to a whole region without naming countries:
      leave EMPTY and use regions instead
  List EVERY country the location mentions. "São Paulo | Bogotá" is ["BR","CO"],
  not just the first one: a person in either country must be able to find it.
  The DESCRIPTION can restrict what the location says: "Remote" plus "must be
  based in the US" means ["US"].
  Never guess a country the posting does not support. Two known traps:
    "Lowell, AR" or any US city followed by AR -> Arkansas, so ["US"], not Argentina
    "Avenue of the Americas"                   -> a street in New York, ["US"]

regions — zero or more of: latam, namerica, emea, apac, global
  latam     Latin America, including Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean.
            Spain and Portugal are NOT latam.
  namerica  United States and Canada
  emea      Europe, Middle East, Africa
  apac      Asia and Pacific
  global    open to anywhere in the world, with no country restriction
  Include the region of every country you listed. Use global only when the
  posting is genuinely open worldwide. "Americas" alone is ambiguous: if it
  lists only the US and Canada, it is namerica, not latam.

eligible — true if a person living somewhere in Latin America could be hired
  for this job. That includes on-site and hybrid jobs located in Latin America,
  and remote jobs open to Latin America or worldwide. false when the posting
  requires residence or work authorization outside Latin America.

is_agency — true when the employer is a staffing, consulting, outsourcing or recruiting
  firm hiring on behalf of a client, rather than hiring for itself.

is_evergreen — true when this is a talent pool, "general interest" or "future
  opportunities" posting rather than a real open role.

note — ONE short sentence IN SPANISH explaining your call. Always explain when
  job_function is "other", when the level was ambiguous, and when the location
  needed interpretation. Maximum 160 characters.`;

const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'OBJECT',
  properties: {
    job_function:   { type: 'STRING', enum: ['engineering','product','design','marketing','sales','operations','support','other'] },
    level:          { type: 'STRING', enum: ['junior','mid','senior','staff','lead','manager','director','vp','unknown'] },
    tags:           { type: 'ARRAY', items: { type: 'STRING', enum: ['backend','frontend','fullstack','mobile','infra','data','ml','ai','security','qa','sap','salesforce'] } },
    suggested_tags: { type: 'ARRAY', items: { type: 'STRING' } },
    work_mode:      { type: 'STRING', enum: ['remote','hybrid','onsite','unknown'] },
    countries:      { type: 'ARRAY', items: { type: 'STRING' } },
    regions:        { type: 'ARRAY', items: { type: 'STRING', enum: ['latam','namerica','emea','apac','global'] } },
    eligible:       { type: 'BOOLEAN' },
    is_agency:      { type: 'BOOLEAN' },
    is_evergreen:   { type: 'BOOLEAN' },
    note:           { type: 'STRING' },
  },
  required: ['job_function','level','tags','suggested_tags','work_mode','countries','regions','eligible','is_agency','is_evergreen','note'],
  propertyOrdering: ['job_function','level','tags','suggested_tags','work_mode','countries','regions','eligible','is_agency','is_evergreen','note'],
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------

const filas = $input.all();

const out = filas.map(i => {
  const j = i.json;

  const posting = [
    `TITLE: ${j.title || ''}`,
    `DEPARTMENT: ${j.department || '(none)'}`,
    `LOCATIONS: ${j.locations || '(none)'}`,
    `DESCRIPTION: ${j.description || '(none)'}`,
  ].join('\n');

  return { json: {
    db_id: j.id,
    external_id: j.external_id,
    title: j.title,
    taxonomy_version: TAXONOMY_VERSION,
    body: {
      systemInstruction: { parts: [{ text: SYSTEM }] },
      contents: [{ role: 'user', parts: [{ text: posting }] }],
      generationConfig: {
        temperature: 0,
        responseMimeType: 'application/json',
        responseSchema: SCHEMA,
      },
    },
  }};
});

console.log('=== PROMPTS ===');
console.log('sin clasificar en esta corrida: ' + out.length);
console.log('ejemplo:\n' +
  (out[0] ? out[0].json.body.contents[0].parts[0].text.slice(0, 400) : '(ninguno)'));

return out;
